page.layout: Running head at top, with page number at top right. Below it, two woodcut medallions side by side, each with a legend around its rim (left: DORA ... THEO; right: SEN CON IMP ... MICHAEL). Then one column of running text with two paragraphs. Below the text, a woodcut ornament without text. No margin notes.

main_text.l: DORA THEO
SEN CON IMP MICHAEL
THEODORA Zoës soror, quæ iam etiam cum ea men-
ses circiter treis imperium tenuerat Constantinopolitanū (vti
in Zoë dixi) nunc denuo, sed sola, post Constantinum Mono-
machum imperat, anno mundi 5017. à Christo nato 1055. Nec
verò est quòd pudeat hanc in ordine ac serie Imperatorum in-
ferere, cùm non muliebriter se gesserit: quinimo tanta domi,
forísque hac imperante quies & ocium fuit, tanta rerum om-
nium ubertas, ut fœminei imperij neminem pœniteret. Verùm
ingrauescente cum ætate morbo, illecebris Eunuchorum ad-
ducta, Michaëlem iam senem imperij ac curæ participem fe-
cit: nec ita diu superuixit: annos propè duos imperauit. Vide
Egna.lib.2.Rom.prin.& Cosmo. Munst. ubi de Græcia tractat,
libro quarto.
MICHAEL senior, post Theodoram supradictam, qua
dixi via, Constantinopoli imperat, anno mundi 5019. à Christi
natiuitate 1057. Fuit quidem hic Michaël genere & opibus
clarus: cætera minus ad imperij fasces ac administrationem
suscipiendam, aut exequendam, idoneus, vel propter ætatem
decrepitam & prægrauantem. Quare cùm vix etiam annum im-
peritasset, Isaacij Comneni factio eum imperio deturbauit, &
in ordinem redegit: priuatus itaque factus, paulò post fatis ac
naturæ concessit. Videto ut supra.

page.notes: Legends of the two medallions are transcribed above. The first letter of DORA on the left coin and the letters of SEN on the right coin are partly cut off by the rim; these are copied as far as visible. The accent on forísque is doubtful. Page number printed in old-style figures. No catchword or signature visible. Bottom woodcut ornament carries no text.
